entities.name: Methyl ester hydrolysis
observations: Decoded product: corresponding compound with C(CC(=O)O) replacing C(CC(=O)OC).
Net transformation is methyl ester de-esterification to carboxylic acid; neutral formula changes from C35H44N3O7P to C34H42N3O7P.
The apparent [P] versus [S] token difference in the raw strings is not present in the decoded molecular structures and should not be interpreted as phosphorus-to-sulfur chemistry.

entities.name: Aqueous lithium hydroxide hydrolysis
observations: Potential condition for methyl ester saponification: LiOH in aqueous THF, aqueous methanol, or aqueous ethanol, typically at ambient to mild heating, followed by acidification.
Often selected for chemoselective ester hydrolysis in multifunctional molecules because amides and ketones are generally retained under controlled conditions.

entities.name: Aqueous sodium hydroxide hydrolysis
observations: Potential condition for methyl ester saponification: dilute NaOH in aqueous alcohol or water, ambient temperature to mild heating, followed by acidic workup.
More forceful than LiOH when concentrated or heated; monitor for degradation of sensitive multifunctional substrate.

entities.name: Acidic ester hydrolysis
observations: Potential alternative: aqueous HCl or sulfuric acid in water/alcohol, usually with heating.
May hydrolyze the methyl ester but is less attractive here because the substrate contains amide, phosphonic-acid, and alcohol functionalities.
